cls: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist - fertility/ovulation control agent
pharm: A synthetic decapeptide that competitively blocks pituitary GnRH receptors, rapidly and reversibly suppressing luteinizing hormone (LH) release and thereby preventing premature LH surges during controlled ovarian stimulation.
quick: 250 micrograms subcutaneously once daily during the mid-to-late follicular phase
Contraindicated - do not use once pregnancy is established
Contraindicated / not for use in nursing mothers
Not studied in renal impairment; short-course use
Not studied in hepatic impairment; short-course use
Ovarian response (ultrasound/estradiol), signs of OHSS, injection-site reactions
summary: Ganirelix acetate is a synthetic GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) antagonist used during controlled ovarian hyperstimulation as part of assisted reproductive technology to prevent premature surges of luteinizing hormone. It is given as a 250 microgram subcutaneous injection once daily, started on day 7 or 8 of follicle-stimulating hormone stimulation (or when follicles reach an appropriate size) and continued daily including the day of hCG administration. By competitively and reversibly blocking pituitary GnRH receptors, it rapidly suppresses LH, avoiding the early ovulation that would compromise oocyte retrieval. It is generally well tolerated; the main risks are local injection-site reactions, hypersensitivity (the product historically contained latex in the needle cap), and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome related to the overall stimulation protocol. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. This monograph is based on the FDA prescribing information for ganirelix acetate.
indications: Inhibition of premature luteinizing hormone (LH) surges in women undergoing controlled ovarian hyperstimulation as part of assisted reproductive technology / fertility treatment

dosage.n: Begin on day 7 or 8 of FSH/gonadotropin stimulation (or when adequate follicular development), continue daily through the day hCG is given

dosage.d: 250 micrograms SC into the abdomen (around the navel) or upper thigh
dosage.n: Rotate injection sites to limit local reactions

admin: Confirm the patient is not pregnant before starting and that gonadotropin (FSH) stimulation has been underway as per protocol
Administer 250 micrograms subcutaneously once daily, ideally at the same time each day, into the abdomen or upper thigh
Rotate injection sites to minimise local irritation, redness and swelling
Begin on stimulation day 7-8 (or when follicles reach the protocol-defined size) and continue daily including the day of hCG trigger
Inspect the solution - use only if clear and colourless; do not mix with other medicines
Be alert for hypersensitivity (historical needle-cap latex); have appropriate management available
moa: Ganirelix is a synthetic decapeptide GnRH antagonist that competitively binds to gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptors on pituitary gonadotrope cells. Unlike GnRH agonists, it produces immediate, dose-dependent suppression of luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone secretion without an initial stimulatory flare. During controlled ovarian hyperstimulation, this rapid, reversible blockade prevents the premature endogenous LH surge that would otherwise trigger early ovulation and luteinization, allowing follicles to mature and be retrieved at the optimal time. Pituitary suppression is reversed quickly after the drug is stopped.

absolute: Known pregnancy (must not be used once pregnancy is established)
Known hypersensitivity to ganirelix, GnRH or any GnRH-analogue, or to any component
relative: Prior hypersensitivity reaction to GnRH analogues
Conditions predisposing to ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
monitor: Follicular development by ultrasound and serum estradiol
Signs and symptoms of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (abdominal distension, pain, breathlessness)

preg: Ganirelix is contraindicated in pregnancy. It is intended for use only before pregnancy is established, during the controlled ovarian stimulation phase. If pregnancy occurs, ganirelix must be discontinued. Animal data showed fetal resorptions at high doses.
lact: It is not known whether ganirelix is excreted in human milk, and it is not intended for use in nursing mothers; it should not be used during breastfeeding.
renal: The pharmacokinetics of ganirelix have not been specifically studied in patients with renal impairment. Because it is used as a short course of daily injections during a single stimulation cycle, no specific dose adjustment is defined.
hepatic: The pharmacokinetics of ganirelix have not been specifically studied in patients with hepatic impairment. Given the short treatment course, no specific dose adjustment is established.

moderate: No formal drug-drug interaction studies have been performed; caution when co-administering with drugs that affect pituitary-gonadal function
minor: Used together with gonadotropins (FSH) and hCG as part of the stimulation protocol (intended combination, not an adverse interaction)
interactions.diagnostics: Suppresses serum LH and FSH (intended effect); affects estradiol response during stimulation monitoring.

serious: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (related to the overall stimulation protocol)
Ectopic pregnancy / congenital anomaly risk inherent to ART
rare: Severe allergic reaction on first dose
emergency: Severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (marked abdominal distension, breathlessness, reduced urine output)

monitoring: Follicular growth by transvaginal ultrasound and serum estradiol during stimulation
Signs and symptoms of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
Hypersensitivity reactions, particularly early in treatment
Confirmation of timing for hCG trigger and oocyte retrieval
counsel: This injection stops your body from releasing an egg too early during your fertility treatment
Inject it under the skin of the abdomen or upper thigh once a day at about the same time, rotating the spot each day
Mild redness or swelling at the injection site is common and usually settles quickly
Report severe abdominal swelling or pain, rapid weight gain, breathlessness, or reduced urination - these may signal overstimulation of the ovaries
Tell your clinic immediately if you develop a rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing after an injection
Use it exactly on the days your clinic instructs, including the day of your trigger injection
pk: Rapid LH suppression within hours of injection
Plasma Tmax approximately 1-2 hours after subcutaneous dosing
Pituitary suppression reverses quickly after the last dose
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from light; do not freeze
pearls: This monograph is based on the FDA prescribing information for ganirelix acetate (a synthetic peptide GnRH antagonist)
Unlike GnRH agonists, ganirelix gives immediate LH suppression with NO initial flare - useful to prevent a premature LH surge in ART
Standard dose is 250 micrograms SC once daily, started on stimulation day 7-8, continued through the hCG trigger day
Watch for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, which relates to the whole stimulation protocol rather than ganirelix alone
Historical formulations had latex in the needle cap - ask about latex allergy; contains mannitol
missed: If a daily dose is missed, contact the fertility clinic for advice as soon as possible; correct timing is important to prevent a premature LH surge. Do not double the dose without clinic instruction.
overdose: There is no clinical experience of overdose in humans. Given its mechanism, overdose would be expected to cause more profound, but still reversible, pituitary suppression of LH and FSH. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive and pituitary function recovers after the drug is stopped.
